META.key_conflicts: The central conflict is swing_mean_reversion (bullish, 38) vs swing_catalyst_news + swing_macro_context (bearish, 65/74). Mean_reversion sees the Fib 50% at $605.89 and RSI-7 at 23 as a valid dip-buy entry for a bounce to $626. Catalyst_news and macro_context view the exact same oversold reading as 'dead-cat bounce risk on a short' — i.e., the bounce to $619–628 IS the short entry, not the long entry. Resolution: this disagreement tells us the trend is extended enough that a bounce is highly probable, but the medium-term direction remains down. The bounce is tradeable as a short setup, not a long. A secondary conflict exists between swing_breakout (neutral, watching $600 for bearish breakdown) and mean_reversion (bullish at $608). Breakout explicitly notes the BB width is too wide for a fresh breakout entry and RSI divergence argues against immediate downside continuation — hence neutral rather than short. This is not a conflict with the bearish thesis; it is a timing disagreement. Swing_trend_momentum is also neutral, waiting for the same $619–628 bounce-rejection candle as catalyst_news and macro_context. The two neutral agents are not disagreeing with bearish direction — they are refusing to short into oversold. This nuance is important: 4 of 5 agents (all except mean_reversion) expect price to bounce into $618–628 before the next leg lower.
